title: Zoning update and 400 Westwood Drive townhomes
subtitle: Both items sent to January 20 Council: new legal administrator position, tree protection, driveways and neighbour concerns.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee dealt with two public hearing items and referred both to the January 20, 2025 Council meeting. Because it is a committee, nothing was finally approved; Council will make the decisions.

The first item was the annual Zoning By-law update, which makes minor and technical changes to the City's two zoning by-laws. It also asked for a new Legal Services Administrator position to support development reviews. The committee referred the whole recommendation so staff can give more information on why the position is needed {{vote:m1}}.

The second item was a request to rezone 400 Westwood Drive to allow five street-fronting townhomes, with a tree protection area covering much of the lot. After hearing from the applicant's planner, a neighbour and a nearby resident, the committee referred it so the applicant, staff and residents can talk further about tree protection, effects on neighbouring properties, the lot pattern and traffic {{vote:m2}}.
Residents will have another chance to be heard at Council.

decisions.item: Annual Zoning By-law Update and new legal position
decisions.detail: The committee referred the proposed amendments to both zoning by-laws and the request for a new Legal Services Administrator position to the January 20, 2025 Council meeting so staff can explain the need for the position.

The committee referred the proposed rezoning for five townhomes to the January 20, 2025 Council meeting to allow further talks on tree protection, effects on abutting properties, lot fabric and traffic.

debate: On the legal position, one councillor said the request was unrelated to the zoning changes and asked for a fuller report, noting that industry had predicted a construction slowdown in 2025. Staff said it would be fully recovered through application fees and that lawyers were doing work better suited to administrative staff. Staff offered to share a time study and lean review before Council.

Staff said the zoning changes are minor and technical. Questions covered building height and what counts as a storey, and when remaining areas under the older by-law would move to the newer one. Staff said changing the 11 metre height limit would need an Official Plan amendment, so it is beyond this update.

A neighbour to the south opposed the Westwood Drive rezoning. The neighbour raised risks to a shared retaining wall and boundary trees, loss of natural screening, a building close to the property line, and the change from low-density zoning. The neighbour asked for a protected buffer along the south boundary and said two or three detached homes would fit the area better. Another resident supported the neighbour and asked whether the south side could be addressed.

The applicant's planner said about two-thirds of the site would be protected, the wooded area has no natural heritage designation, and the city's arborist review raised no further concerns. Staff said the tree protection by-law would not apply to a lot this size, so the owner could otherwise remove trees. Staff said a note about removing the neighbour's retaining wall was a mistake and only the wall on the subject lands would be removed.

Councillors asked about a single shared driveway, which staff said does not fit with the shallow front yards. The planner said driveways might be paired later to keep more on-street parking. Councillors also asked about moving the units north to add a south buffer. Staff said a grove of maples to the north needs protecting, and that the rental replacement by-law applies only to six or more units.
